findings.passage: In his veto message, the governor said the measure would create an obstacle to voting, resulting in fewer people casting ballots and “undermining our democracy.”
findings.note: AP report on his veto of the photo-ID bill SB 2. The sentence is the reporter's summary of his veto message with two words quoted from it.

findings.passage: “The fact that someone would need something to vote that right now they absolutely can’t get because of the coronavirus, yes, I think is a wrong move, and it absolutely needed to be vetoed,” Beshear said at his daily coronavirus-related briefing.
findings.note: Quoted by AP at his briefing: objects to requiring an ID that offices were closed and could not issue during the pandemic.

findings.passage: “Furthermore, no documented evidence of recent voter fraud in the form of impersonation in Kentucky has been presented in support of Senate Bill 2 and, therefore, the legislation would be attempting to resolve a problem does not exist,” Beshear wrote.
findings.note: Quoted from his written veto message on SB 2 (WVXU, Ryland Barton): says no evidence of voter impersonation was presented.
Vetoed SB 2, which required a photo ID to vote, with a sworn-affidavit route using a non-photo document and a free ID at county clerks' offices; the legislature later overrode the veto.

Vetoed 2025 HB 684, an elections bill; the legislature's bill page lists a governor's veto message and veto override steps. A local news report says his message objected to reversing a 2020 rule that let voters show a debit or credit card as ID at the polls. Veto text itself was not read.

findings.passage: Asked about how the new executive order could impact Kentucky voters, Beshear said in his Thursday press conference that “it shouldn’t affect Kentuckians because it is wholly and entirely unconstitutional.”
findings.note: On the federal order limiting mail voting and having a list of citizens compiled for states; he calls it unconstitutional. Related topic: mail-ballot rules, citizen lists.

findings.passage: “It was a full and fair election. That's a fact. Period,” Beshear said.
findings.note: Related remark at his weekly briefing: says Kentucky elections are secure and rejects claims about 2020. Does not address ID or citizenship directly.
